title: arXiv Trending Physics — Monthly — 2026-10-30
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart; this ordering is inferred from independent coverage, cross-field/reproducibility signals and recency, while citation evidence is limited for such recent preprints.

sections.title: Meter-scale quantum interconnects between large quantum processors
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate four microwave L-couplers bridging two 120-qubit superconducting processors, with high-fidelity state transfer and remote entangling gates.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report four 80-cm superconducting links between two IBM Nighthawk R1 processors, 99.00% mean state-transfer fidelity and 94.75% mean remote CZ-gate fidelity, including simultaneous Bell-pair generation.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; four superconducting coax links, network benchmarking and remote-gate tests on two 120-qubit processors
sections.unique_caveat: This is a demonstration on one pair of modules with four links; the mean remote CZ fidelity is 94.75%, and the paper describes the magnetic shielding used for the cables as temporary.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three independent October write-ups from Quantum Brief, The Quantum Insider and Herald discuss the result and its measured transfer/gate fidelities.

sections.title: A Control Line Multiplexing Framework for Scalable Quantum Computing
sections.announcement_type: new submission; updated to v3 within the window
sections.abstract: The authors propose and demonstrate frequency-division-multiplexed microwave control for parallel single- and two-qubit gates, sharing control resources across four operations without a statistically significant multiplexing penalty.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report mean errors of (6.4±0.2)×10⁻³ for four parallel frequency-multiplexed CZ gates and (10.6±0.2)×10⁻⁴ for parallel XY(π/2) gates, with no statistically significant degradation versus dedicated controls; the larger line-count reductions are projections.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; 1:4 frequency-division-multiplexing test of microwave gates on a superconducting processor, supplemented by architecture simulations
sections.unique_caveat: The experimental multiplexing ratio is 1:4. The paper’s 1/12 line-count estimate and 1/48 idealized estimate are projections, not demonstrations on a large processor or a full cryogenic network.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Near-contemporaneous technical coverage from Quantum Crier and Quantum Zeitgeist corroborates the new 1:4 gate-control result; arXiv records updates through v3 on 28 October.

sections.title: High Resolution Hyperspectral Quantum Infrared Imaging with Undetected Photons
sections.abstract: The team demonstrates folded nonlinear-interferometer transmission imaging around 1550 nm using undetected photons, with phase-stepped spectral readout of a zebrafish larva and a printed target.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 1550-nm transmission imaging with about 74% maximum baseline visibility and a resolving power of ~1460 from the spectrometer point-spread function; the coherence-length estimate is ~730, over an instantaneous window of about 51 cm⁻¹.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; folded spontaneous-parametric-down-conversion interferometer, with raster-scanned images of a fixed zebrafish larva and a carbon-ink logo
sections.unique_caveat: The setup is a laboratory point-by-point demonstration with ~1-mm spatial resolution; its two spectral-resolution estimates differ (4.4 cm⁻¹ by spectrometer PSF versus 8.9 cm⁻¹ by coherence length), and it does not establish medical imaging performance.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Independent technical coverage at QubitWire and Quentir describes the laboratory demonstration and distinguishes it from a clinical or field-ready imager.

sections.title: Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor
sections.abstract: The study tests rotated surface-code memory on IBM’s Nighthawk r2 processor, combining shorter readout, fused measurement/reset and echo control to reduce logical errors while identifying degradation and correlations in longer memories.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that, with the other code distance fixed at 3, increasing protected distance from 3 to 6 reduces per-round error from 0.53% to 0.24% in Z memory and 0.52% to 0.22% in X memory over short runs; optimized syndrome extraction also lowers median errors relative to the standard circuit.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; rotated surface-code memory runs on IBM Nighthawk r2, with circuit comparisons and maximum-likelihood/minimum-weight decoding
sections.unique_caveat: In experiments extending to 150 rounds, the distance advantage weakens as long-lived syndrome correlations build up; the authors leave the source of the persistent component unresolved.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Quantum Crier published an October 16 technical summary highlighting the cloud-accessible hardware result and the same code-distance and circuit-optimization measurements.

sections.title: Optimal robust single-qubit gates in superconducting quantum processors
sections.abstract: The authors experimentally demonstrate time-rescaled robust inverse-optimal pulses for superconducting-transmon gates designed to tolerate simultaneous drive-amplitude and frequency-detuning errors.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 90-ns X gates above 99.9% fidelity and above 99.5% fidelity under simultaneous drive-amplitude variations up to 20% and detuning up to 4 MHz; Hadamard-type gates exceed 99.6% in their tests.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; interleaved randomized benchmarking and quantum-process tomography on a superconducting transmon processor, with numerical pulse-design analysis
sections.unique_caveat: The experiment controls one qubit in a small two-transmon processor; the authors note increased leakage for shorter pulses and identify higher-bandwidth control and leakage mitigation as follow-up needs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Quantum Computing Report covered the TRIO pulse result and its quantified robustness against combined calibration errors.

sections.title: Femtosecond Three-Dimensional Imaging of Single-Protein with Hard X-ray Laser
sections.abstract: Using hard-X-ray free-electron-laser pulses, the team reconstructs three-dimensional diffraction images of single giant-hemoglobin erythrocruorin complexes, with lower 3D than 2D resolution likely related to sample heterogeneity.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 2D diffraction classes reconstructed to 15 Å and 3D images at approximately 20–30 Å for single erythrocruorin complexes using hard-X-ray laser pulses.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; single-particle diffraction at the European XFEL SPB/SFX instrument, with 3D reconstruction and molecular-dynamics analysis of possible compaction
sections.unique_caveat: The 3D reconstruction is less resolved than the 2D classes; the authors attribute the discrepancy likely to heterogeneity from gas-phase compaction, so native-state ultrafast structural dynamics remain a prospect, not a result here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The v3 revision appeared on 24 October; the authors released experimental data through European XFEL and analysis code, and the paper is cross-listed across five physics subjects. No independent news feature was found in sources checked, so it ranks below papers with broader external coverage.
